summary.text: Mike Flood is the Republican incumbent for Nebraska's 1st Congressional District. A Norfolk attorney and broadcast company founder, he served in the Nebraska Legislature, including as Speaker, before winning a June 2022 special election to the U.S. House. He serves on the House Financial Services Committee and is seeking another term after advancing unopposed from the 2026 Republican primary.

paragraphs.text: Born in Omaha, Nebraska, and raised in Norfolk, where he graduated from Norfolk Catholic High School in 1993.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Notre Dame in 1997 and a law degree from the University of Nebraska in 2001.

Began working in radio in high school; in 1999 founded Flood Communications, which his official biography says grew from one Norfolk radio station into a statewide media network including News Channel Nebraska.
Works as a broadcaster and attorney.

Elected to the Nebraska Legislature in 2005 to represent Madison County (District 19) and served until 2013; his colleagues elected him Speaker in 2007, which his official biography describes as the youngest in state history.
Returned to the Legislature after winning the 2020 election for District 19 and served from 2021 to 2022.
Won the June 28, 2022 special election for Nebraska's 1st District with 52.7% of the vote over Democrat Patty Pansing Brooks, succeeding Jeff Fortenberry, and was sworn in July 12, 2022.
Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services, where his official biography says he chairs the Housing and Insurance Subcommittee, and chairs the Republican Main Street Caucus.
Has served as chairman of the board of the Children's Scholarship Fund and on the board of Invest Nebraska, and is a member of the U.S. Strategic Command Consultation Committee.
According to his official biography, lives in Norfolk with his wife, Mandi, and their sons Brenden and Blake.
